from that may Agni and Indra, being in accord, release us!
Whatever unpaid debt [remains] from me here, by which pledge of Yama we wander,
here, O Agni, I become free from debt; living indeed, I repay the debts from my hands!
Whatever wrongs I have committed with my hands, smelling the clamor of the dice, O waters,
and from Ugraṃpaśya and Rāṣṭrabhṛt, those debts let loose to the Apsarases [be cleared]!
May Ugraṃpaśya [and] Rāṣṭrabhṛt [remove] the wrongs, whatever roll of dice has been yielded here;
lest indebted, he seeking our debts [takes us]; a deposit in the world of Yama for imperishability.
Hear this call of mine, O Varuṇa, and be gracious today;
desiring help, I long for you.
With prayer, praising you, I ask for that; the sacrificer hopes for that with oblations.
Being without wrath here, O Varuṇa, take note! O wide-praised one, do not steal away our lifespan!
Loosen the uppermost bond from us, O Varuṇa, [loosen] down the lowest, loosen apart the middle one;
then may we, O Āditya, in your ordinance, be sinless for Aditi!
Away your wrath, O Varuṇa, with reverences, away with sacrifices [and] oblations we seek;
dwelling [here] for us, O wise Asura, O king, loosen the sins committed!
Knowing [this], O Agni, you should turn away from us the wrath of the god Varuṇa;
most sacrificial, best conveyer, blazing brightly, release from us all hostilities!
So, O Agni, be closest to us with help, nearest at the dawning of this dawn;
turn Varuṇa away for us, being generous; seek mercy, be easy for us to invoke!
Saṃkasuka, Vikasuka, Nirṛta, and Nisvana,
remove the consumption far, far away from us, who are sinless!
He has removed consumption; he made the witchcraft Nirṛti.
Whoever clashes with us by that, to him we drive it away!
With ill-spoken word and repeated spoken word, with the club and the repeated club,
whoever clashes with us by that, to him we drive it away!
We have united with radiance, with milk, with bodies, with auspicious thought.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the good giver, distribute wealth; may he wipe away what is damaged in our bodies.

4.14.18.s: śucī vo havyā marutaḥ śucīnāṃ śuciṃ hinomy adhvaraṃ śucibhyaḥ | ṛtena satyam ṛtasāpa āyañ śucijanmānaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ || yā vaḥ śarma śaśamānāya santi || aṃseṣv ā marutaḥ khādayo vo vakṣaḥsu rukmā upaśiśriyāṇāḥ | vi vidyuto na vṛṣṭibhī rucānā anu svadhām āyudhair yachamānāḥ || ṛṣṭayo vo maruto aṃsayor adhi || ime turaṃ maruto rāmayantīme sahaḥ sahasā ānamanti | ime śaṃsaṃ vanuṣyato nipānti guru dveṣo araruṣe dadhanti || arā ived acaramā aheva praprajāyante akavā mahobhiḥ || pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ svayā matyā marutaḥ saṃmimikṣuḥ || agnīṣomā imaṃ yuvam etāni || agnīṣomā yo adya vām idaṃ vacaḥ saparyati | tasmai dhattaṃ suvīryaṃ gavāṃ poṣaṃ svaśvyam || ānyaṃ divo mātariśvā jabhārāmathnād anyaṃ pari śyeno adreḥ | agnīṣomā brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānoruṃ yajñāya cakrathur ulokam || agnīṣomā ya āhutiṃ yo vāṃ dāśād dhaviṣkṛtim | sa prajayā suvīryaṃ viśvam āyur vyaśnavat || agnīṣomā haviṣaḥ prasthitasya vītaṃ haryataṃ vṛṣaṇā juṣethām | suśarmāṇā svavasā hi bhūtam athā dhattaṃ yajamānāya śaṃ yoḥ || ā carṣaṇiprā vṛṣabho janānāṃ rājā kṛṣṭīnāṃ puruhūta indraḥ | stutaḥ śravasyann avasopa madrig yuktvā harī vṛṣaṇāyāhy arvāk || viveṣa yan mā dhiṣaṇā jajāna || taṃ sadhrīcīr ūtayo vṛṣṇyāni pauṃsyāni niyutaḥ saścur indram | samudraṃ na sindhava ukthaśuṣmā uruvyacasaṃ girā āviśanti || satyam it tan na tvāvaṃ anyo 'stīndra devo na martyo jyāyān | ahann ahiṃ pariśayānam arṇo 'vāsṛjo apo achā samudram || prasasāhiṣe puruhūta śatrūn || sa śevṛdham adhidhā dyumnam asme mahi kṣatraṃ janāṣāḍ indra tavyam | rakṣā ca no maghonaḥ pāhi sūrīn rāye ca naḥ svapatyā iṣe dhāḥ ||
4.14.18.d: शुची वो हव्या मरुतः शुचीनां शुचिं हिनोम्य् अध्वरं शुचिभ्यः । ऋतेन सत्यम् ऋतसाप आयञ् शुचिजन्मानः शुचयः पावकाः ॥ या वः शर्म शशमानाय सन्ति ॥ अंसेष्व् आ मरुतः खादयो वो वक्षःसु रुक्मा उपशिश्रियाणाः । वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचाना अनु स्वधाम् आयुधैर् यछमानाः ॥ ऋष्टयो वो मरुतो अंसयोर् अधि ॥ इमे तुरं मरुतो रामयन्तीमे सहः सहसा आनमन्ति । इमे शंसं वनुष्यतो निपान्ति गुरु द्वेषो अररुषे दधन्ति ॥ अरा इवेद् अचरमा अहेव प्रप्रजायन्ते अकवा महोभिः ॥ पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः संमिमिक्षुः ॥ अग्नीषोमा इमं युवम् एतानि ॥ अग्नीषोमा यो अद्य वाम् इदं वचः सपर्यति । तस्मै धत्तं सुवीर्यं गवां पोषं स्वश्व्यम् ॥ आन्यं दिवो मातरिश्वा जभारामथ्नाद् अन्यं परि श्येनो अद्रेः । अग्नीषोमा ब्रह्मणा वावृधानोरुं यज्ञाय चक्रथुर् उलोकम् ॥ अग्नीषोमा य आहुतिं यो वां दाशाद् धविष्कृतिम् । स प्रजया सुवीर्यं विश्वम् आयुर् व्यश्नवत् ॥ अग्नीषोमा हविषः प्रस्थितस्य वीतं हर्यतं वृषणा जुषेथाम् । सुशर्माणा स्ववसा हि भूतम् अथा धत्तं यजमानाय शं योः ॥ आ चर्षणिप्रा वृषभो जनानां राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इन्द्रः । स्तुतः श्रवस्यन्न् अवसोप मद्रिग् युक्त्वा हरी वृषणायाह्य् अर्वाक् ॥ विवेष यन् मा धिषणा जजान ॥ तं सध्रीचीर् ऊतयो वृष्ण्यानि पौंस्यानि नियुतः सश्चुर् इन्द्रम् । समुद्रं न सिन्धव उक्थशुष्मा उरुव्यचसं गिरा आविशन्ति ॥ सत्यम् इत् तन् न त्वावं अन्यो ऽस्तीन्द्र देवो न मर्त्यो ज्यायान् । अहन्न् अहिं परिशयानम् अर्णो ऽवासृजो अपो अछा समुद्रम् ॥ प्रससाहिषे पुरुहूत शत्रून् ॥ स शेवृधम् अधिधा द्युम्नम् अस्मे महि क्षत्रं जनाषाड् इन्द्र तव्यम् । रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीन् राये च नः स्वपत्या इषे धाः ॥
4.14.18.m:
Pure are your oblations, O Maruts, [the oblations] of the pure ones; I speed the pure sacrifice to the pure ones.
Attending truth, by truth they came to reality, pure of birth, pure, purifying.
Which shelters of yours are there for the zealous one...
On your shoulders, O Maruts, are bangles, on your chests golden ornaments are resting;
shining like lightnings with rains, holding out their weapons according to their own nature.
Spears are on your shoulders, O Maruts...
These Maruts halt the swift one; these bend power by power;
these protect from the curse of the assailant; they place heavy hatred on the non-giver.
Like spokes indeed, not last, like days they bring forth, not deficient in greatness.
The highest, most vehement sons of Pṛśni, the Maruts have mingled by their own thought.
O Agni-and-Soma, this [sacrifice]...
You both these [lights]...
O Agni-and-Soma, whoever serves this word of yours today,
to him grant good manly strength, thriving of cattle, good horses!
The one Mātariśvan brought from heaven, the other the falcon churned around the rock;
O Agni-and-Soma, grown great through the sacred utterance, you made broad space for the sacrifice.
O Agni-and-Soma, whoever presents an oblation to you, who performs sacrificial offering,
may he attain full span of life with offspring, with good manly strength!
O Agni-and-Soma, accept the oblation set forth, take pleasure, enjoy, O two bulls!
For become of good shelter and good aid, then grant welfare and blessing to the sacrificer!
Fulfilling the peoples, the bull of folk, king of the peoples, much-invoked Indra—
praised, longing for renown, come hither towards me with aid, having yoked the two bay stallion steeds!
When the bowl bore me, it entered...
Allied aids, virile powers, manly deeds, and teams have accompanied that Indra;
like rivers to the ocean, those whose strength is the solemn verse enter with song the one of wide expansion.
True indeed is that: there is no other like you, Indra, neither god nor mortal is greater!
You slew the serpent lying around the flood; you released the waters towards the ocean.
You have conquered the enemies, O much-invoked one...
Establish for us wealth increasing friendliness, great dominion, O Indra conquering men, mighty one;
and protect our patrons, guard our lords, and set us in wealth, good offspring, and vigor!
